{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BwS114HQttjArZSwwD45Ub","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Patagonia Health — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-14\n     4→Developer website: https://patagoniahealth.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Patagonia Health is a privately held healthcare IT company founded in 2009 by Ashok Mathur, headquartered in Cary, North Carolina. The company builds an integrated cloud-based EHR, practice management, and billing platform specifically designed for **public health departments** and **behavioral health agencies**. This is a niche-focused vendor — rather than serving general ambulatory or hospital settings, Patagonia Health targets local/county health departments, statewide public health systems, school-based health clinics, and community behavioral health organizations.\n     9→\n    10→The company claims to cover 60M+ lives across 38+ states and 510+ counties, with $622M+ in claims processed. They report a 98% client retention rate and have won consecutive Stevie Awards for customer service since 2015. Patagonia Health is a Certified NC Minority-Owned business. Notable customers include Fairfax County Health Department (Virginia), Cleveland County Health Department, Beaufort County Health Department, and Richmond and Stokes County Health Departments (North Carolina). The vendor appears to be mid-size, serving the public/behavioral health niche rather than competing with large general-purpose EHR vendors.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Patagonia Health EHR\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11147\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Patagonia Health EHR is a cloud-based, web-delivered SaaS application that combines electronic health records, practice management, billing, telehealth, and a patient portal into a single integrated platform. The product is specifically designed for public health and behavioral health workflows — not a general ambulatory EHR repurposed for these settings. It requires only a modern web browser and internet connection (no VPN or local installation needed). The certified module (Patagonia Health EHR Version 6) appears to be the full product — there is no indication that this is a subset of a larger platform. The certification covers 35+ criteria spanning clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10), indicating a comprehensive clinical system.\n    19→\n    20→### Users & Market\n    21→\n    22→**Primary customer segments:**\n    23→- **Local/county health departments** — the core market. These organizations handle immunizations, communicable disease surveillance, contact tracing, community outreach, and general public health services.\n    24→- **Statewide and federal health systems** — multi-location deployments with centralized reporting and a statewide master patient index.\n    25→- **Behavioral health agencies** — therapists, counselors, psychiatrists, clinical directors, and supervisors in community mental health and substance use treatment settings.\n    26→- **School-based health programs** — clinics operating in school settings.\n    27→\n    28→**Day-to-day users** include clinicians (physicians, nurses, therapists, counselors, psychiatrists), clinical directors/supervisors, billing staff, front desk/registration staff, practice managers, and public health administrators. Patients interact through the MyHealth patient portal.\n    29→\n    30→The product is positioned for small-to-medium organizations — county health departments, community behavioral health agencies — though it also scales to statewide deployments. Pricing starts at ~$500/user/month with modular scaling.\n    31→\n    32→### Modules & Functionality\n    33→\n    34→Based on vendor website, feature pages, third-party reviews, and case studies:\n    35→\n    36→**Electronic Health Record (Clinical Documentation)**\n    37→- Customizable clinical templates (described as configurable to match paper forms the organization was previously using)\n    38→- Write-in sections for custom clinical information\n    39→- Document upload functionality\n    40→- Electronic charting with multiple input methods\n    41→- Clinical quality measures (CQM) tracking and reporting\n    42→- Support for behavioral health-specific documentation: psychiatric assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, group notes, case management notes\n    43→- DSM-5 coding support (DSM V database referenced on technology page)\n    44→\n    45→**E-Prescribing**\n    46→- Medication selection from extensive database\n    47→- Automatic drug interaction and allergy checking\n    48→- Secure electronic transmission to pharmacies\n    49→- Surescripts connectivity implied by e-prescribing certification criteria\n    50→\n    51→**Lab Integration**\n    52→- Lab order management\n    53→- Lab results viewing for clinicians and patients\n    54→- Interfaces with LabCorp, Solstas, and Quest Diagnostics (per technology page)\n    55→\n    56→**Immunization & Public Health Programs**\n    57→- Vaccine inventory tracking\n    58→- Immunization registry synchronization with state registries\n    59→- Communicable disease surveillance and tracking\n    60→- Contact tracing support\n    61→- Community outreach program management\n    62→- Support for mobile off-site clinics\n    63→- State-specific program eligibility and reporting (e.g., HRSA UDS clearinghouse transactions.\n   133→\n   134→**Patient portal data:** Secure messages between patients and providers, patient-completed questionnaires, self-reported demographic updates, portal notification history.\n   135→\n   136→**Communication data:** eFax records, Direct messages, HIE transactions, lab interface messages.\n   137→\n   138→**Reporting/analytics data:** Clinical quality measure calculations, UDS reports, state/federal/county compliance reports, custom report definitions, dashboard configurations.\n   139→\n   140→The product uses standard clinical terminologies (ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED, RxNorm, DSM-5) and supports CCDA 2.1 and FHIR data formats for interoperability.\n   141→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be The vendor appears to be mid-size, serving the public/behavioral health niche rather than competing with large general-purpose EHR vendors.\n\n## Product: Patagonia Health EHR\n\nCHPL ID: 11147\n\n### What It Is\n\nPatagonia Health EHR is a cloud-based, web-delivered SaaS application that combines electronic health records, practice management, billing, telehealth, and a patient portal into a single integrated platform. The product is specifically designed for public health and behavioral health workflows — not a general ambulatory EHR repurposed for these settings. It requires only a modern web browser and internet connection (no VPN or local installation needed). The certified module (Patagonia Health EHR Version 6) appears to be the full product — there is no indication that this is a subset of a larger platform. The certification covers 35+ criteria spanning clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10), indicating a comprehensive clinical system.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Primary customer segments:**\n- **Local/county health departments** — the core market. These organizations handle immunizations, communicable disease surveillance, contact tracing, community outreach, and general public health services.\n- **Statewide and federal health systems** — multi-location deployments with centralized reporting and a statewide master patient index.\n- **Behavioral health agencies** — therapists, counselors, psychiatrists, clinical directors, and supervisors in community mental health and substance use treatment settings.\n- **School-based health programs** — clinics operating in school settings.\n\n**Day-to-day users** include clinicians (physicians, nurses, therapists, counselors, psychiatrists), clinical directors/supervisors, billing staff, front desk/registration staff, practice managers, and public health administrators. Patients interact through the MyHealth patient portal.\n\nThe product is positioned for small-to-medium organizations — county health departments, community behavioral health agencies — though it also scales to statewide deployments. Pricing starts at ~$500/user/month with modular scaling.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, feature pages, third-party reviews, and case studies:\n\n**Electronic Health Record disease surveillance and tracking\n- Contact tracing support\n- Community outreach program management\n- Support for mobile off-site clinics\n- State-specific program eligibility and reporting (e.g., {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01MVx4P8kE7BiaubxqfYXfsp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B67N66vRcVPVFz6xWGC4su","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat /tmp/patagonia-page.html | python3 -c \"\nimport sys, re\nhtml = sys.stdin.read()\n# Remove script and style tags\nhtml = re.sub(r'<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\\1>', ' ', html, flags=re.DOTALL|re.IGNORECASE)\n# Replace tags with newlines for block elements\nhtml = re.sub(r'<(br|p|div|h[1-6]|li|tr|td|th)[^>]*>', '\\n', html, flags=re.IGNORECASE)\n# Remove all remaining tags\nhtml = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', html)\n# Collapse whitespace\nhtml = re.sub(r'[ \\t]+', ' ', html)\n# Collapse multiple newlines\nhtml = re.sub(r'\\n\\s*\\n+', '\\n', html)\nprint(html.strip()[:5000])\n\"","description":"Extract clean text from HTML"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2497,"cache_read_input_tokens":42754,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2497},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"b61d6a8a-cf82-44c7-a973-aa1f4983f3ac"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_018aWSdtKaBw5PQfWX9uCQSr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015D3EndZfps1QZGKLeik7UH","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 -c \"\nimport re\nwith open('/tmp/patagonia-page.html') as f:\n    html = f.read()\nhtml = re.sub(r'<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\\1>', ' ', html, flags=re.DOTALL|re.IGNORECASE)\nhtml = re.sub(r'<(br|p|div|h[1-6]|li|tr|td|th)[^>]*>', '\\n', html, flags=re.IGNORECASE)\nhtml = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', html)\nhtml = re.sub(r'[ \\t]+', ' ', html)\nhtml = re.sub(r'\\n\\s*\\n+', '\\n', html)\nprint(html.strip()[:8000])\n\"","description":"Extract visible text from HTML page"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":458,"cache_read_input_tokens":45251,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":458},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"0f3d12ce-a454-4a59-9529-cad5529fd61b"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015D3EndZfps1QZGKLeik7UH","type":"tool_result","content":"ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT | Patagonia Health \n &lt;img src=\"https://www.instinct-agilebusiness.com/806375.png\" style=\"display:none;\"&gt; \n CLIENTS\n Tech Support\n Client Sales\n SEARCH\n SOLUTIONS \n EHR Solutions \n Practice Management \n Billing \n Telehealth \n Patient Portal \n WHO WE SERVE \n Overview \n Public Health Departments \n Behavioral Health Agencies \n Federal Statewide Solutions \n School-Based Health \n WHY US \n Why Patagonia Health? \n Patient Experience \n Technology \n Academy \n ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT \n ONC Real World Testing \n RESOURCES \n Success Stories \n Articles \n Webinars \n Educational Resources \n ABOUT US \n Meet Our Team \n Awards \n CONTACT \n REQUEST A DEMO\n ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT \nPatagonia Health EHR Version 6 \nPatagonia Health’s EHR version 6 is ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT compliant under the Drummond Group’s Electronic Health Records Office of the National Coordinator Authorized Certification Body program. \nWhat does this mean for you? \n Promoting Interoperability places an emphasis on improving interoperability and patients’ access to health information. \n Patagonia Health implementation&nbsp; makes it easy &nbsp;for providers to achieve the next level of compliance without any changes in their regular workflow. \n Connections with other providers using Direct Messaging, Health Information Exchange and CCDA exchange on a patient portal are readily available. Clinical Quality Measures (CQMs) are automatically tracked. \n Patagonia Health EHR Classification Type is fully certified to meet 100 percent of general criteria and all required clinical quality criteria. To verify certification status and learn more, click&nbsp; here . \nCertification verifies the EHR software adheres to the privacy and security HIPAA laws and can work with other systems to share information. \n&nbsp; \nAn Overview of Meaningful Use \nIn 2009, the HITECH Act, part of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, made $17 billion of funding available for financial incentive payments for the “meaningful use” of EHRs by eligible providers, eligible hospitals and critical access hospitals (CAHs) who participate in Medicare and Medicaid. In order to meet Meaningful Use (MU) requirements, these providers are required to demonstrate that they are using their EHR technology in a significant way, both quantitatively and qualitatively, and that this impact can be proved by meeting a number of set objectives. \nFor a department or practice to receive federal EHR incentives, the following are major considerations: \n The EHR system must meet Meaningful Use/Promoting Interoperability requirements (EHR vendor’s responsibility). \nTo be eligible for incentives, a provider must use an Electronic Health Record software that meets federal requirements for ARRA-defined Meaningful Use/Promoting Interoperability. Each eligible provider attesting for Modified Stage 2 must comply with 10 objectives and 6 clinical quality measures. Each provider attesting for Stage 3 must comply with 8 objectives and 9 clinical quality measures. Patagonia Health EHR meets 100% of these requirements and is certified for receiving EHR incentives. \n The EHR must be federally certified (EHR vendor responsibility). \nThe EHR must be certified by a federally Authorized Testing &amp; Certification Body (ATCB). Patagonia Health’s complete EHR version 6 is certified by the Drummond Group (an ATCB) for ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT.&nbsp; \n An EHR must be in use by each eligible provider. \nFederal agencies want to encourage the&nbsp; use &nbsp;of an EHR, not just a purchase! Each eligible provider is required to use the EHR to perform certain functions like electronic prescriptions, viewing lab results, etc. Patagonia Health EHR has removed the complexity of federal compliance for provider practices and agencies by incorporating all the requirements into normal provider workflows. In addition, Patagonia Health EHR provides an easy to use reports for practices and agencies to track their progress towards required compliance. \nPatagonia Health’s team is knowledgeable and is committed to working with their customers to make sure practices qualify and receive their due incentives. \n&nbsp; \nCMS oversees the Medicare EHR Incentive Program, and the state Medicaid agencies manage the Medicaid EHR Incentive Program. While the two programs are similar, there are some key differences between them. The tabs below give an overview of each program. Additional Patagonia Health video tutorials and webcasts on federal compliance can be found in the Resources section, our video library and additional resources are also listed below. \nMedicaid EHR Incentive Program \n Run by Your State Medicaid Agency \n Program runs from 2011 through 2021 \n Maximum incentive amount is $63,750 \n Payments over 6 years, do not have to be consecutive \n No payment adjustments for providers who are only eligible for the Medicaid program \n In the first year, providers can receive an incentive payment for adopting, implementing or upgrading EHR technology. Providers must demonstrate Meaningful Use in the remaining years to receive incentive payments. \n An “eligible professional” is defined as:\n A doctor of medicine or osteopathy \n A doctor of dental surgery or medicine \n A certified nurse-midwife \n A nurse practitioner \n Physician Assistants practicing in an FQHC or RHC that is so led by a physician assistant \nTo qualify for participation, the Eligible Professional must also meet one of the following criteria: \n Have a minimum 30% Medicaid patient volume* \n Have a minimum of 20% Medicaid patient volume, and be a pediatrician* \n Practice predominantly in a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or Rural Health Clinic (RHC) and have a minimum of 30% patient volume attributable to needy individuals \nMedicaid Patient Volume Requirements: 30% of patients seen in a 90-day period in the previous calendar year should be Medicaid enrollees. \n*Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) patients do not count toward the Medicaid patient volume criteria. \n&nbsp; \nDrummond Group Certification \n This Health IT module is compliant with the ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. This certification does not represent an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Drummond Group is accredited by ANSI and approved by ONC for the ONC Health IT Certification Program to certify: Health IT Module(s) and Certification of other types of Health IT for which the Secretary has adopted certification criteria under Subpart C of 45 CFR. \nCriteria Tested: 170.315 (a)(1-5, 12, 14); (b)(1-3, 10-11); (c)(1-3); (d)(1-9, 11-13); (e)(1, 3); (f)(1-2, 5); (g)(2-7, 9-10) \nClinical Quality Measures tested: 2v6; 68v6; 69v5; 117v5; 122v5; 124v5; 128v5; 130v5; 134v5; 138v5; 146v5; 159v5; 161v5; 164v5; 165v5; 177v5 \nAdditional software used: NewCrop eRx, EMR Direct Interoperability Engine \n &gt;&gt; Download Certificate \n&nbsp; \nAny additional types of costs that an EP, EH, or CAH would pay to implement the Complete EHR’s capabilities in order to attempt to meet Meaningful Use objectives and measures. EHR technology self-developers are excluded from this requirement. \n &gt;&gt;View Supplemental Costs \n&nbsp; \n&nbsp; \nElectronic Health Information (EHI) Export \n&nbsp; \nEHI Export \nThe capability of EHI export within Patagonia EMR is based on role based access to EHI export reporting and billing role. Users with access to EHI export permission will have the ability to execute an EHI export for clinical data. Billing User role will help user the ability to extract patient financial export and claims data export. \n&nbsp; \nEnabling Access to EHI Export \nA Practice Administrator can enable access roles for specific users under: \nPractice Administration &gt; Staff Management &g","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"48970ab0-d430-4cdf-be15-9fbebd181d0e","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT | Patagonia Health \n &lt;img src=\"https://www.instinct-agilebusiness.com/806375.png\" style=\"display:none;\"&gt; \n CLIENTS\n Tech Support\n Client Sales\n SEARCH\n SOLUTIONS \n EHR Solutions \n Practice Management \n Billing \n Telehealth \n Patient Portal \n WHO WE SERVE \n Overview \n Public Health Departments \n Behavioral Health Agencies \n Federal Statewide Solutions \n School-Based Health \n WHY US \n Why Patagonia Health? \n Patient Experience \n Technology \n Academy \n ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT \n ONC Real World Testing \n RESOURCES \n Success Stories \n Articles \n Webinars \n Educational Resources \n ABOUT US \n Meet Our Team \n Awards \n CONTACT \n REQUEST A DEMO\n ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT \nPatagonia Health EHR Version 6 \nPatagonia Health’s EHR version 6 is ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT compliant under the Drummond Group’s Electronic Health Records Office of the National Coordinator Authorized Certification Body program. \nWhat does this mean for you? \n Promoting Interoperability places an emphasis on improving interoperability and patients’ access to health information. \n Patagonia Health implementation&nbsp; makes it easy &nbsp;for providers to achieve the next level of compliance without any changes in their regular workflow. \n Connections with other providers using Direct Messaging, Health Information Exchange and CCDA exchange on a patient portal are readily available. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XtHMFZjTWmZydKc8MtZWVS","type":"tool_result","content":"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export \n&nbsp; \nEHI Export \nThe capability of EHI export within Patagonia EMR is based on role based access to EHI export reporting and billing role. Users with access to EHI export permission will have the ability to execute an EHI export for clinical data. Billing User role will help user the ability to extract patient financial export and claims data export. \n&nbsp; \nEnabling Access to EHI Export \nA Practice Administrator can enable access roles for specific users under: \nPractice Administration &gt; Staff Management &gt; Edit Selected User &gt;&nbsp;&nbsp;EHI Export&nbsp;&amp;&nbsp;Schedule Data Export. \nAfter you select a User, click&nbsp;Edit Selected User \nSelect EHI Export \n&nbsp; \nSingle Patient EHI Export \nData export is available in the EHR’s Reports section. \nReports &gt; Medical Practice Reports &gt; Select Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export \nAll practice providers are covered. However, individual providers can be selected. Blank date ranges will cover the entire span of patient encounters. Specific date ranges can also be entered.&nbsp; \nEnter a specific patient name for EHI export. Click Search. \nSelect the Patient Record and click EHI Export. When the export file is generated, it can be downloaded to your local system. The format of the clinical data is CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1. \nTo extract the billing data associated with the patient, go to Dashboard &gt; Billing &gt; Search &gt; Claims. \nClaim data can then be downloaded in CSV or&nbsp; XLSX formats for computation. \n&nbsp; \nMulti-Patient EHI Export \nData export is available in the EHR’s Reports page. \nReports &gt; Medical Practice Reports &gt; Select&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;Electronic Health Information (EHI) ExportClick the&nbsp;Multi Patients&nbsp;button in the Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export Report \nClick Start task on and set an appropriate date and time for the Export task to execute and click Save \nExporting all patients may take some time. The export Status will be updated from Queued to Completed when the task is finished. \nTo extract the billing data for patients, go to Dashboard &gt; Billing &gt; Reports &gt; Claim &gt; Detail. \nSet fields Claim Receive Date, Claim Service Date, and Claim Submitted Date to All. \nRun report. Export data in CSV or XLSX formats for computation. \n&nbsp; \nExported File Formats \nClinical data is exported as CCDA (XML) \nBilling data is exported as CSV, XLSX, or PDF. \nPatient Health Data API and FHIR Access \n Patient Health Data API Documentation v1.1 \n SmartON FHIR API Documentation \n FHIR Service Base URLs \nPatagonia Health, Inc. \n15100 Weston Parkway\nSuite #204\nCary, North Carolina 27513 \n (919) 238-4780 \n SOLUTIONS \n Electronic Health Records \n Practice Management \n Billing \n Patient Portal \n Telehealth \n ABOUT US \n Meet Our Team \n Awards \n Request a Demo \n Contact \n WHO WE SERVE \n Overview \n Public Health Departments \n Behavioral Health Agencies \n Federal &amp; Statewide Solutions \n School-Based Health \n WHY US \n Why Patagonia Health? \n Patient Experience \n Technology \n Academy \n ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT \n ONC Real World Testing \n RESOURCES \n Success Stories \n Articles \n Webinars \n Educational Resources \n 10 years running\n Privacy Policy \n Cookie Policy \n Terms &amp; Conditions \nCopyright © 2026 Patagonia Health, Inc, all rights reserved.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"00ff16fc-7773-46ee-8fa9-13bf04e65434","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export \n&nbsp; \nEHI Export \nThe capability of EHI export within Patagonia EMR is based on role based access to EHI export reporting and billing role. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TbGg8j7aQ8CHDAcwXDSRs9","type":"tool_result","content":"Patagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\n\nPatagonia Health EHR Patient Data Access API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nIntroduction\nThis document describes Patagonia Health EHR API for patient data access. Registered users can use this API to query\nthe EHR for patient data. The API returns a JSON object with status and embedded CCDA XML. API examples below show\nhow to access the API using curl.\n\nRequirements\nUser must be an authorized user of the Patagonia Health EHR or user must have access to the Patagonia Health patient\nportal\nAccess to REST client (use curl, or any other programmatic REST client)\nAbility to parse JSON and CCDA\n\nAPI\nFollowing sections describe the available API. URL for accessing the API is\nhttps://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/\n\nAuthenticate user\nUse your credentials to Patagonia Health EHR or Patagonia Health Patient Portal to authenticate with the API. API\nreturns a token that will be used for all other API calls.\nUser name and password have to encoded in Base64 with the call to curl. Use Basic authorization header for curl.\nExample:\n\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Authorization: Basic\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/authenticateuser'\nResponse:\n{\"TokenID\":\" 6b972240-2692-4002-a9f4-cf11031dfbde \"}\nStore the value TokenID. That TokenID will be used for all further calls to API\nPage | 1\n15100 Weston Parkway #204Cary, North Carolina 27513\nPhone 919.622.6740info@patagoniahealth.com\n\n\fPatagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\n\nSearch for a patient\nSearch for a patient from EHR using one or more parameters list below\n• MRN\n• Date of birth\n• First name\n• Last name\nAPI will search for patients that match one or more these criteria and return up to 30 patients.\nExamples:\nSearch using MRN:\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Token: NmI5NzIyNDAtMjY5Mi00MDAyLWE5ZjQtY2YxMTAzMWRmYmRl'\n'Authorization: Basic\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/patientsearch?mrn=MR1234\n5’\nResponse:\n{\n\"PatagoniaHealthPatientList\" : [{\n\"AddressLine1\" : \"1357, Amber Dr\",\n\"AddressLine2\" : \"\",\n\"City\" : \"Beaverton\",\n\"DateOfBirth\" : \"5\\/1\\/1970\",\n\"EmailAddress\" : \"phehr2008@gmail.com\",\n\"FirstName\" : \"Alice\",\n\"Gender\" : \"F\",\n\"HomePhoneNumber\" : \"(555)555-1544\",\n\"LastName\" : \"Newman\",\n\"MRN\" : \"MR12345\",\n\"MiddleName\" : \"Jones\",\n\"State\" : \"OR\",\n\"Zipcode\" : \"97006\"\n}\n],\n\"Result\" : \"Success: Found 1 patients\"\n}\nSearch using last name and date of birth (dob)\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Token: NmI5NzIyNDAtMjY5Mi00MDAyLWE5ZjQtY2YxMTAzMWRmYmRl'\n'Authorization: Basic\nPage | 2\n15100 Weston Parkway #204Cary, North Carolina 27513\nPhone 919.622.6740info@patagoniahealth.com\n\n\fPatagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\n\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/patientsearch?lastname=s\nmith&dob=2000-01-01’\nResponse\n2 patients are found that match the date of birth and last name\n{\n\"PatagoniaHealthPatientList\" : [{\n\"AddressLine1\" : \"1357, Amber Dr\",\n\"AddressLine2\" : \"\",\n\"City\" : \"Beaverton\",\n\"DateOfBirth\" : \"01\\/1\\/2000\",\n\"EmailAddress\" : \"\",\n\"FirstName\" : \"Alice\",\n\"Gender\" : \"F\",\n\"HomePhoneNumber\" : \"\",\n\"LastName\" : \"Smith\",\n\"MRN\" : \"MR22345\",\n\"MiddleName\" : \"\",\n\"State\" : \"OR\",\n\"Zipcode\" : \"97006\"\n},\n{\n\"AddressLine1\" : \"234, Main St\",\n\"AddressLine2\" : \"\",\n\"City\" : \"Beaverton\",\n\"DateOfBirth\" : \"01\\/1\\/2000\",\n\"EmailAddress\" : \"\",\n\"FirstName\" : \"Jane\",\n\"Gender\" : \"F\",\n\"HomePhoneNumber\" : \"\",\n\"LastName\" : \"Smith\",\n\"MRN\" : \"MR32345\",\n\"MiddleName\" : \"\",\n\"State\" : \"OR\",\n\"Zipcode\" : \"97006\"\n}\n],\n\"Result\" : \"Success: Found 2 patients\"\n}\nFind the correct patient. Use that patient’s MRN returned from these calls for remaining API\n\nPage | 3\n15100 Weston Parkway #204Cary, North Carolina 27513\nPhone 919.622.6740info@patagoniahealth.com\n\n\fPatagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\n\nGet Patient CCDA\nRequest the entire CCDA for a patient, using the following command\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Token: NmI5NzIyNDAtMjY5Mi00MDAyLWE5ZjQtY2YxMTAzMWRmYmRl'\n'Authorization: Basic\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/patientCCDA?mrn=MR12345’\nResponse\n\n<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<ClinicalDocument xmlns:xsd=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema\"\nxmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance\" moodCode=\"EVN\"\nxmlns=\"urn:hl7-org:v3\" xmlns:sdtc=\"urn:hl7-org:sdtc\">\n<code code=\"34133-9\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.6.1\" codeSystemName=\"LOINC\"\ndisplayName=\"Summarization of Episode Note\" />\n<effectiveTime value=\"20180225114039-0500\" />\n<confidentialityCode code=\"N\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.5.25\" />\n<languageCode code=\"en-US\" />\n<recordTarget>\n<patientRole>\n<id root=\"2.16.840.1.113883.4.1\" extension=\"MR12345\" />\n<addr use=\"HP\">\n<streetAddressLine>1357, Amber Dr</streetAddressLine>\n<city>Beaverton</city>\n<state>OR</state>\n<postalCode>97006</postalCode>\n</addr>\n<telecom value=\"tel:(555)723-1544\" use=\"HP\" />\n<telecom value=\"tel:(555)777-1234\" use=\"MC\" />\n<patient>\n<name use=\"L\">\n<given>Alice</given>\n<given>Jones</given>\n<family>Newman</family>\n</name>\n<administrativeGenderCode code=\"F\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.5.1\"\ncodeSystemName=\"AdministrativeGender\" displayName=\"Female\" />\n<birthTime value=\"19700501\" />\n<maritalStatusCode code=\"M\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.5.2\"\ncodeSystemName=\"MaritalStatus\" displayName=\"Married\" />\n<raceCode code=\"2106-3\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.6.238\"\ncodeSystemName=\"Race and Ethnicity- CDC\" displayName=\"White\" />\n<ethnicGroupCode code=\"2186-5\" codeSystem=\"2.16.840.1.113883.6.238\"\ncodeSystemName=\"Race and Ethnicity Code Sets\" displayName=\"Not Hispanic/Latino\"\n/>\n<languageCommunication>\n<languageCode code=\"en\" />\nPage | 4\n15100 Weston Parkway #204Cary, North Carolina 27513\nPhone 919.622.6740info@patagoniahealth.com\n\n\fPatagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\n</languageCommunication>\n</patient>\n</patientRole>\n</recordTarget>\n<!-- Standard CCDA elements here -->\n</ClinicalDocument>\n\nGet patient CCDA for a limited time range\nIn order to get records for a specific time period, use the same service with start date and end date parameters\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Token: NmI5NzIyNDAtMjY5Mi00MDAyLWE5ZjQtY2YxMTAzMWRmYmRl'\n'Authorization: Basic\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/patientCCDA?mrn=MR12345&\nstartDate=2016-01-01&endDate=2018-01-01’\nStart and end date are formatted as YYYY-MM-DD. The command above queries for data between Jan 1 2016 (2016-0101) and Jan 1 2018 (2018-01-01)\nResponse will be the same CCDA as above, except the encounters will be restricted to date of service between Jan 1\n2016 and Jan 1 2018.\n\nGet Clinical Sections\nRequest specific clinical sections from a patient’s CCDA using the following command format\ncurl -X POST -k -H 'Token: NmI5NzIyNDAtMjY5Mi00MDAyLWE5ZjQtY2YxMTAzMWRmYmRl'\n'Authorization: Basic\ncGF0YWdvbmlhaGVhbHRodXNlcm5hbWU6MmphJERpcFVVJXdjNFdTKnoxT1E=' -i\n'https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/patientData\n?mrn=MR12345&sectionName=<sectionName for API>’\nIn the command above, “sectionName for API” can be one of the following\nsectionName value provided to API\nClinical Section returned by API\nall\nAll\ndemographics\nPatient Demographics\ncareteam\nCare Team\nallergies\nAllergies and Intolerances\nassessments\nAssessment\nencounters\nEncounters\nfunctionalstatus\nFunctional Status\ngoals\nGoals\nhealthconcerns\nHealth Concerns\nPage | 5\n15100 Weston Parkway #204Cary, North Carolina 27513\nPhone 919.622.6740info@patagoniahealth.com\n\n\fPatagonia Health EHR API\nDocumentation\nVersion 1.1 April 2018\n\nwww.patagoniahealth.com\nimmunizations\nmedicalequipment\nmedications\nmentalstatus\nplanoftreatment\nproblem\nprocedures\nreasonforreferral\nresults\nsocialhistory\nvitalsigns\n\nImmunizations\nMedical Equipment\nMedications\nMental Status\nPlan of Treatment\nProblem\nProcedures\nReason for Referral\nResults\nSocial History\nVital Signs\n\nExample:\nIf sectionName=demographics, following CCDA will EHR v6\nINTRODUCTION\n\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access protected health information based on the documentation of an open API. The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization (Ref. https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/ )\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\n\n•\n\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.phemr.co/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.phemr.co/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication\n\n•\n\nPublic Clients\n\nSteps for Smart App Launch\n1.\n\nClient App Registration\n\n2.\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\n\n3.\n\nObtain authorization code\n\n4.\n\nObtain access token\n\n5.\n\nAccess FHIR API\n\n6.\n\nRefresh Token to obtain new access token\n\n\fClient APP Registration\nBefore a SMART app can run against an EHR, the app must be registered with that EHR’s authorization service. We are using OAuth 2.0 Client\nRegistration.\n\nClient App Request process\n•\n\nThird-party application must sign the API Subscription Agreement with following details\no\no\no\no\no\n\n•\n\nThe app name\nThe necessary APIs / Scopes\nAny redirect URIs\nLaunch_URL (optional)\nURL to JWK Set (Only for apps supporting asymmetric client authentication).\n\nThe application is created by the EHR admin after confirming the app’s registration parameters and communicates a client_id to the\napp.\no FHIR APIs (of any supported version) listed within the USCDI v3 core data set will be supported\no Only reads data from FHIR server\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\nIn order to obtain launch context and request authorization to access FHIR resources, the app discovers the EHR FHIR server’s SMART\nconfiguration metadata, including OAuth authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint URLs.\nFHIR server makes SMART configuration available from well-known endpoint. You can get Authorization end point and token endpoint.\n\nRequest\nGET 200 https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/.well-known/smart-configuration\n\nResponse\n{\n\"capabilities\": [\n\"launch-ehr\",\n\"launch-standalone\",\n\"client-public\",\n\"client-confidential-symmetric\",\n\"sso-openid-connect\",\n\"context-banner\",\n\"context-style\",\n\"context-ehr-patient\",\n\"context-ehr-encounter\",\n\"context-standalone-patient\",\n\"context-standalone-encounter\",\n\"permission-offline\",\n\"permission-patient\",\n\"permission-user\"\n],\n\"revocation_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/token/revoke-token\",\n\"authorization_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/authorization\",\n\"token_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/token\"\n}\n\nError codes\nJSON response is returned from the FHIR Server along with the code\n200: Ok\n401: Unauthorized\n400: Bad Request\n500: Internal Server Error\n\n\fObtain authorization code\nThe app supplies the following parameters to the EHR’s “authorize” endpoint.\n\nParameters\n\nresponse_type\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization (Ref. https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/ )\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\n\n•\n\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.phemr.co/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.phemr.co/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication\n\n•\n\nPublic Clients\n\nSteps for Smart App Launch\n1.\n\nClient App Registration\n\n2.\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\n\n3.\n\nObtain authorization code\n\n4.\n\nObtain access token\n\n5.\n\nAccess FHIR API\n\n6.\n\nRefresh Token to obtain new access token\n\n\fClient APP Registration\nBefore a SMART app can run against an EHR, the app must be registered with that EHR’s authorization service. We are using OAuth 2.0 Client\nRegistration.\n\nClient App Request process\n•\n\nThird-party application must sign the API Subscription Agreement with following details\no\no\no\no\no\n\n•\n\nThe app name\nThe necessary APIs / Scopes\nAny redirect URIs\nLaunch_URL (optional)\nURL to JWK Set (Only for apps supporting asymmetric client authentication).\n\nThe application is created by the EHR admin after confirming the app’s registration parameters and communicates a client_id to the\napp.\no FHIR APIs (of any supported version) listed within the USCDI v3 core data set will be supported\no Only reads data from FHIR server\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\nIn order to obtain launch context and request authorization to access FHIR resources, the app discovers the EHR FHIR server’s SMART\nconfiguration metadata, including OAuth authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint URLs.\nFHIR server makes SMART configuration available from well-known endpoint. You can get Authorization end point and token endpoint.\n\nRequest\nGET 200 https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/.well-known/smart-configuration\n\nResponse\n{\n\"capabilities\": [\n\"launch-ehr\",\n\"launch-standalone\",\n\"client-public\",\n\"client-confidential-symmetric\",\n\"sso-openid-connect\",\n\"context-banner\",\n\"context-style\",\n\"context-ehr-patient\",\n\"context-ehr-encounter\",\n\"context-standalone-patient\",\n\"context-standalone-encounter\",\n\"permission-offline\",\n\"permission-patient\",\n\"permission-user\"\n],\n\"revocation_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/token/revoke-token\",\n\"authorization_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/authorization\",\n\"token_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.phemr.co/outh/token\"\n}\n\nError codes\nJSON response is returned from the FHIR Server along with the code\n200: Ok\n401: Unauthorized\n400: Bad Request\n500: Internal Server Error\n\n\fObtain authorization code\nThe app supplies the following parameters to the EHR’s “authorize” endpoint.\n\nParameters\n\nresponse_type\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: code.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01Kx8Kk5JR4UzKfoeEJNHJt4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017ZR9gPNAjEBSRnjVxHRDni","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/patagonia-health/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Patagonia Health — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-14\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://patagoniahealth.com/onc-certified-hit\n- CHPL IDs: 11147\n- Product: Patagonia Health EHR Version 6\n- Certification date: 2022-12-27\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n### Step 1: Initial probe\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://patagoniahealth.com/onc-certified-hit\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nHTTP/2 200. Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8. Hosted on HubSpot CMS behind Cloudflare. No redirects — the registered URL is a live HubSpot-hosted page.\n\n### Step 2: Fetch and examine page\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/onc-certified-hit\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/patagonia-page.html\n```\n50,851 bytes. Static HTML page (not a SPA). The page is the vendor's ONC certification information page containing sections on Meaningful Use, Drummond Group certification, and EHI Export. The EHI Export section appears near the bottom, under its own `<h2>` heading.\n\n### Step 3: Identify downloadable files\nExtracted all `href` links. Found the following relevant downloadable files:\n- `/hubfs/Certifications/PatientHealth-Data-API-Documentation-v1.1.pdf` — Patient Health Data API Documentation v1.1\n- `/hubfs/SmartOnFHIR-API-Documentation.pdf` — SmartOnFHIR API Documentation (67 pages)\n- `/hubfs/FHIRBaseURL.json` — FHIR Service Base URLs (JSON Bundle)\n- `/hubfs/Certifications/PatagoniaHealth-MeaningfulUse-Stage3-CostsandLimitations-May2018.pdf` — Supplemental costs and limitations\n- `/hubfs/Certifications/Compliance%20Certificate%20Patagonia%20Health%20EHR%206%20122924.pdf` — Compliance certificate (not downloaded — no EHI export content)\n\n### Step 4: Browser screenshots\nNavigated to the page in Chrome, scrolled to the \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\" section, and took screenshots capturing the full EHI documentation section.\n\n### Step 5: Downloaded all linked files\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/Certifications/PatientHealth-Data-API-Documentation-v1.1.pdf\" -o PatientHealth-Data-API-Documentation-v1.1.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/SmartOnFHIR-API-Documentation.pdf\" -o SmartOnFHIR-API-Documentation.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/FHIRBaseURL.json\" -o FHIRBaseURL.json\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/Certifications/PatagoniaHealth-MeaningfulUse-Stage3-CostsandLimitations-May2018.pdf\" -o PatagoniaHealth-MeaningfulUse-Stage3-CostsandLimitations-May2018.pdf\n```\nAll files verified with `file` command — confirmed actual PDF documents and valid JSON.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### EHI Export Documentation (on the web page)\n\nThe EHI export documentation lives entirely inline on the ONC certification page, under the heading \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export.\" There is no separate PDF, data dictionary, or downloadable spec for the EHI export itself — the documentation is approximately 400 words of inline HTML describing the export workflow.\n\n**Export mechanism:** The EHI export is accessed within the EHR's Reports section:\n- **Single Patient:** Reports > Medical Practice Reports > Select Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export. The user selects a provider (or all), optionally sets date ranges, searches for a specific patient, selects the record, and clicks \"EHI Export.\" The export file is generated and downloaded locally.\n- **Multi-Patient:** Same path but using a \"Multi Patients\" button. The user sets a scheduled date/time for execution; the export runs asynchronously with status tracking (Queued → Completed).\n\n**Clinical data format:** CCDA 2.1 Release 2, USCDI v1 (XML).\n\n**Billing data:** Handled separately. For single-patient billing: Dashboard > Billing > Search > Claims. For multi-patient billing: Dashboard > Billing > Reports > Claim > Detail, with options to set Claim Receive Date, Claim Service Date, and Claim Submitted Date to \"All.\" Billing data exports in CSV, XLSX, or PDF.\n\n**Access control:** Role-based. A Practice Administrator enables \"EHI Export & Schedule Data Export\" permissions for specific users under Practice Administration > Staff Management > Edit Selected User. A separate billing role is needed for financial data extraction.\n\n### Patient Health Data API Documentation v1.1 (PDF, 7 pages)\n\nA REST API for patient data access, dated April 2018. This is a proprietary (non-FHIR) API that returns CCDA XML embedded in JSON responses. Endpoints:\n- `authenticateuser` — authenticate with Basic auth, returns a TokenID\n- `patientsearch` — search by MRN, DOB, first/last name (returns up to 30 patients)\n- `patientCCDA` — get full CCDA for a patient by MRN, with optional date range\n- `patientData` — get specific CCDA sections by name (demographics, allergies, assessments, encounters, goals, immunizations, medications, problems, procedures, results, vitals, etc.)\n\nBase URL: `https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/`\n\nThis API predates the FHIR (g)(10) requirement and appears to be the vendor's original data access mechanism. The data returned is limited to what CCDA 2.1 can represent.\n\n### SmartOnFHIR API Documentation (PDF, 67 pages)\n\nThis is the (g)(10) Standardized API documentation, not the (b)(10) EHI export. It documents the SMART on FHIR implementation with OAuth 2.0 authorization and FHIR R4 resources. Resources covered:\n- Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition (Problems/Health Concerns), Device, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Goal, Immunization, Medication, MedicationDispense, Observation (labs, vitals, smoking status), Organization, Procedure, Provenance, ServiceRequest, Coverage, Specimen, RelatedPerson\n\nFHIR endpoint: `https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/`\nAuth server: `https://oauth.phemr.co/`\n\nSupports standalone, EHR-embedded, and backend services (bulk) launch types. This is standard US Core / USCDI scope — not a comprehensive EHI export.\n\n### FHIR Base URLs (JSON, 4.8 KB)\n\nA FHIR Bundle of type \"collection\" containing Endpoint and Organization resources for two test/sample organizations. This is the service base URL listing required by the (g)(10) API — not EHI export-specific.\n\n### Supplemental Costs and Limitations (PDF)\n\nDated May 2018. Documents costs and technical limitations for MU Stage 3 capabilities (Direct Messaging, transitions of care, etc.). Not directly related to EHI export.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nPatagonia Health EHR is a comprehensive platform for public health departments and behavioral health agencies, storing clinical, administrative, billing, and specialty-specific data across many domains. The EHI export documentation reveals a significant gap between what the product stores and what the export covers.\n\n**What the clinical export covers (via CCDA 2.1 / USCDI v1):**\n- Demographics\n- Problems/conditions\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Immunizations\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs\n- Procedures\n- Encounters\n- Care plans/goals\n- Clinical notes (to the extent CCDA supports them)\n- Social history\n- Assessments, functional status, mental status\n\n**What the billing export covers (separate CSV/XLSX workflow):**\n- Claims data\n- Financial/billing records\n\n**What appears to be missing or undocumented:**\n- **Behavioral health assessments** — The product stores psychiatric evaluations, DSM-5 coded diagnoses, treatment plans, progress notes, group therapy notes, and case management notes. CCDA 2.1 has limited support for behavioral health-specific structured data. There is no mention of how these specialty assessments are represented in the export.\n- **Public health program data** — Communicable disease surveillance records, contact tracing data, immunization registry data, vaccine inventory tracking, community outreach records, program eligibility determinations. This is core to the product's public health market. None of this is addressed in the export documentation.\n- **Custom clinical templates** — The product advertises configurable templates matching paper forms. How custom form data is exported (or whether it is) is not documented.\n- **Document uploads** — The product supports document uploads to patient charts. No mention of these in the export.\n- **Patient portal data** — Secure messages, patient-completed questionnaires, consent forms.\n- **Scheduling and referrals** — Appointment records, referral tracking, case management records.\n- **E-prescribing history** — Prescription transmission records beyond medication lists.\n- **Lab orders** — The CCDA may capture results but order details and interface messages are not discussed.\n- **Telehealth encounter data** — Virtual visit recordings or session metadata.\n\nThe fundamental issue is that the clinical EHI export is **CCDA 2.1 constrained to USCDI v1**, which is essentially the same data the (g)(10) FHIR API already provides. This is a textbook case of the (b)(10) vs (g)(10) confusion: the vendor is using their clinical summary document (CCDA) as the EHI export, which only covers the standard clinical data subset. The billing data export is handled separately in a different workflow, which at least acknowledges that EHI is broader than clinical summaries — but the overall approach still leaves many data domains undocumented or unexported.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n**Clinical data:** CCDA 2.1 Release 2, USCDI v1 (XML). This is a well-understood standard, but it constrains the export to clinical summary data. A CCDA cannot represent vaccine inventory, disease surveillance records, program eligibility data, custom form data, or the many other data types this public health / behavioral health EHR stores.\n\n**Billing data:** CSV, XLSX, or PDF. No schema, field definitions, or data dictionary is provided for the billing export. The documentation merely says claims data \"can then be downloaded\" in these formats.\n\n**Appropriateness:** For a general ambulatory EHR, CCDA might cover most clinical data. For a public health and behavioral health EHR with extensive specialty data (communicable disease tracking, behavioral health assessments, DSM-5 coding, program compliance), CCDA is a poor fit. A database dump or structured CSV export of all tables would be far more appropriate for capturing the breadth of data this product manages.\n\nA third party receiving this export would get a standard patient clinical summary and raw billing CSV files, but would not be able to reconstruct the full patient record as it exists in the system.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe EHI export documentation is minimal — roughly 400 words of inline text on a certification page. There is:\n- **No data dictionary** — no description of what fields/tables are included in the export\n- **No schema or format specification** for the billing CSV/XLSX exports\n- **No worked examples** or sample export files\n- **No field-level documentation** — nothing about data types, value sets, cardinality, or constraints beyond \"CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1\"\n- **No description of what CCDA sections are included** in the EHI export specifically (the Patient Health Data API doc lists sections, but this is a different mechanism)\n\nA developer trying to import this data would need to: (1) understand CCDA 2.1 for clinical data (feasible but the vendor provides no custom profile info), and (2) reverse-engineer the billing CSV/XLSX format with no documentation at all.\n\nThe documentation reads as procedural instructions for EHR users (\"click here, then here\") rather than technical documentation of the export format and content. It looks like a compliance checkbox rather than a genuine attempt to document data portability.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** The documentation provides zero field-level detail. No table names, no column names, no data types, no value set documentation.\n- **Relationships:** No description of how clinical and billing data relate, or how to correlate records across the two separate export workflows.\n- **Versioning:** No version or change history for the export documentation itself. The Patient Health Data API doc is labeled v1.1 (April 2018), but the EHI export section has no date or version.\n- **Coded fields:** No documentation of value sets, code systems, or coding conventions used in the billing exports.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://patagoniahealth.com/onc-certified-hit\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (all content is in static HTML; browser used for screenshots only)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (EHI section is inline on the page, scroll to find it)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but no blocking)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone significant. The page loaded cleanly via curl and in the browser. All linked files downloaded without authentication or special headers. The only complication is that the EHI export documentation is entirely inline on the page rather than in a downloadable document, making it easy to miss among the other certification content. There are no images embedded in the EHI section (no screenshots of the export interface), though the text describes the UI workflow steps.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":309,"cache_read_input_tokens":69093,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":309},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"46d75c5a-98c6-4458-9178-b356a44bf909"}

`/hubfs/Certifications/Compliance%20Certificate%20Patagonia%20Health%20EHR%206%20122924.pdf` — Compliance certificate (not downloaded — no EHI export content)\n\n### Step 4: Browser screenshots\nNavigated to the page in Chrome, scrolled to the \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\" section, and took screenshots capturing the full EHI documentation section.\n\n### Step 5: Downloaded all linked files\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/Certifications/PatientHealth-Data-API-Documentation-v1.1.pdf\" -o PatientHealth-Data-API-Documentation-v1.1.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/SmartOnFHIR-API-Documentation.pdf\" -o SmartOnFHIR-API-Documentation.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/FHIRBaseURL.json\" -o FHIRBaseURL.json\ncurl -sL \"https://patagoniahealth.com/hubfs/Certifications/PatagoniaHealth-MeaningfulUse-Stage3-CostsandLimitations-May2018.pdf\" -o PatagoniaHealth-MeaningfulUse-Stage3-CostsandLimitations-May2018.pdf\n```\nAll files verified with `file` command — confirmed actual PDF documents and valid JSON.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### EHI Export Documentation (on the web page)\n\nThe EHI export documentation lives entirely inline on the ONC certification page, under the heading \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export.\" There is no separate PDF, data dictionary, or downloadable spec for the EHI export itself — the documentation is approximately 400 words of inline HTML describing the export workflow.\n\n**Export mechanism:** The EHI export is accessed within the EHR's Reports section:\n- **Single Patient:** Reports > Medical Practice Reports > Select Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export. The user selects a provider (or all), optionally sets date ranges, searches for a specific patient, selects the record, and clicks \"EHI Export.\" The export file is generated and downloaded locally.\n- **Multi-Patient:** Same path but using a \"Multi Patients\" button. The user sets a scheduled date/time for execution; the export runs asynchronously with status tracking (Queued → Completed).\n\n**Clinical data format:** CCDA 2.1 Release 2, USCDI v1 (XML).\n\n**Billing data:** Handled separately. For single-patient billing: Dashboard > Billing > Search > Claims. For multi-patient billing: Dashboard > Billing > Reports > Claim > Detail, with options to set Claim Receive Date, Claim Service Date, and Claim Submitted Date to \"All.\" Billing data exports in CSV, XLSX, or PDF.\n\n**Access control:** Role-based. A Practice Administrator enables \"EHI Export & Schedule Data Export\" permissions for specific users under Practice Administration > Staff Management > Edit Selected User. A separate billing role is needed for financial data extraction.\n\n### Patient Health Data API Documentation v1.1 (PDF, 7 pages)\n\nA REST API for patient data access, dated April 2018. This is a proprietary (non-FHIR) API that returns CCDA XML embedded in JSON responses. Endpoints:\n- `authenticateuser` — authenticate with Basic auth, returns a TokenID\n- `patientsearch` — search by MRN, DOB, first/last name (returns up to 30 patients)\n- `patientCCDA` — get full CCDA for a patient by MRN, with optional date range\n- `patientData` — get specific CCDA sections by name (demographics, allergies, assessments, encounters, goals, immunizations, medications, problems, procedures, results, vitals, etc.)\n\nBase URL: `https://phapi.patagoniaemr.com:31015/PatientService.svc/`\n\nThis API predates the FHIR (g)(10) requirement and appears to be the vendor's original data access mechanism. The data returned is limited to what CCDA 2.1 can represent.\n\n### SmartOnFHIR API Documentation (PDF, 67 pages)\n\nThis is the (g)(10) Standardized API documentation, not the (b)(10) EHI export. It documents the SMART on FHIR implementation with OAuth 2.0 authorization and FHIR R4 resources. Resources covered:\n- Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition (Problems/Health Concerns), Device, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Goal, Immunization, Medication, MedicationDispense, Observation (labs, vitals, smoking status), Organization, Procedure, Provenance, ServiceRequest, Coverage, Specimen, RelatedPerson\n\nFHIR endpoint: `https://fhir.phemr.co:9443/fhirserver/fhir/`\nAuth server: `https://oauth.phemr.co/`\n\nSupports standalone, EHR-embedded, and backend services (bulk) launch types. This is standard US Core / USCDI scope — not a comprehensive EHI export.\n\n### FHIR Base URLs (JSON, 4.8 KB)\n\nA FHIR Bundle of type \"collection\" containing Endpoint and Organization resources for two test/sample organizations. This is the service base URL listing required by the (g)(10) API — not EHI export-specific.\n\n### Supplemental Costs and Limitations (PDF)\n\nDated May 2018. Documents costs and technical limitations for MU Stage 3 capabilities (Direct Messaging, transitions of care, etc.). Not directly related to EHI export.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nPatagonia Health EHR is a comprehensive platform for public health departments and behavioral health agencies, storing clinical, administrative, billing, and specialty-specific data across many domains. The EHI export documentation reveals a significant gap between what the product stores and what the export covers.\n\n**What the clinical export covers (via CCDA 2.1 / USCDI v1):**\n- Demographics\n- Problems/conditions\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Immunizations\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs\n- Procedures\n- Encounters\n- Care plans/goals\n- Clinical notes (to the extent CCDA supports them)\n- Social history\n- Assessments, functional status, mental status\n\n**What the billing export covers (separate CSV/XLSX workflow):**\n- Claims data\n- Financial/billing records\n\n**What appears to be missing or undocumented:**\n- **Behavioral health assessments** — The product stores psychiatric evaluations, DSM-5 coded diagnoses, treatment plans, progress notes, group therapy notes, and case management notes. CCDA 2.1 has limited support for behavioral health-specific structured data. There is no mention of how these specialty assessments are represented in the export.\n- **Public health program data** — Communicable disease surveillance records, contact tracing data, immunization registry data, vaccine inventory tracking, community outreach records, program eligibility determinations. This is core to the product's public health market. None of this is addressed in the export documentation.\n- **Custom clinical templates** — The product advertises configurable templates matching paper forms. How custom form data is exported (or whether it is) is not documented.\n- **Document uploads** — The product supports document uploads to patient charts. No mention of these in the export.\n- **Patient portal data** — Secure messages, patient-completed questionnaires, consent forms.\n- **Scheduling and referrals** — Appointment records, referral tracking, case management records.\n- **E-prescribing history** — Prescription transmission records beyond medication lists.\n- **Lab orders** — The CCDA may capture results but order details and interface messages are not discussed.\n- **Telehealth encounter data** — Virtual visit recordings or session metadata.\n\nThe fundamental issue is that the clinical EHI export is **CCDA 2.1 constrained to USCDI v1**, which is essentially the same data the (g)(10) FHIR API already provides. This is a textbook case of the (b)(10) vs (g)(10) confusion: the vendor is using their clinical summary document (CCDA) as the EHI export, which only covers the standard clinical data subset. The billing data export is handled separately in a different workflow, which at least acknowledges that EHI is broader than clinical summaries — but the overall approach still leaves many data domains undocumented or unexported.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n**Clinical data:** CCDA 2.1 Release 2, USCDI v1 (XML). This is a well-understood standard, but it constrains the export to clinical summary data. A CCDA cannot represent vaccine inventory, disease surveillance records, program eligibility data, custom form data, or the many other data types this public health / behavioral health EHR stores.\n\n**Billing data:** CSV, XLSX, or PDF. No schema, field definitions, or data dictionary is provided for the billing export. The documentation merely says claims data \"can then be downloaded\" in these formats.\n\n**Appropriateness:** For a general ambulatory EHR, CCDA might cover most clinical data. For a public health and behavioral health EHR with extensive specialty data (communicable disease tracking, behavioral health assessments, DSM-5 coding, program compliance), CCDA is a poor fit. A database dump or structured CSV export of all tables would be far more appropriate for capturing the breadth of data this product manages.\n\nA third party receiving this export would get a standard patient clinical summary and raw billing CSV files, but would not be able to reconstruct the full patient record as it exists in the system.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe EHI export documentation is minimal — roughly 400 words of inline text on a certification page. There is:\n- **No data dictionary** — no description of what fields/tables are included in the export\n- **No schema or format specification** for the billing CSV/XLSX exports\n- **No worked examples** or sample export files\n- **No field-level documentation** — nothing about data types, value sets, cardinality, or constraints beyond \"CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1\"\n- **No description of what CCDA sections are included** in the EHI export specifically (the Patient Health Data API doc lists sections, but this is a different mechanism)\n\nA developer trying to import this data would need to: (1) understand CCDA 2.1 for clinical data (feasible but the vendor provides no custom profile info), and (2) reverse-engineer the billing CSV/XLSX format with no documentation at all.\n\nThe documentation reads as procedural instructions for EHR users (\"click here, then here\") rather than technical documentation of the export format and content. It looks like a compliance checkbox rather than a genuine attempt to document data portability.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** The documentation provides zero field-level detail. No table names, no column names, no data types, no value set documentation.\n- **Relationships:** No description of how clinical and billing data relate, or how to correlate records across the two separate export workflows.\n- **Versioning:** No version or change history for the export documentation itself. The Patient Health Data API doc is labeled v1.1 (April 2018), but the EHI export section has no date or version.\n- **Coded fields:** No documentation of value sets, code systems, or coding conventions used in the billing exports.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://patagoniahealth.com/onc-certified-hit\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (all content is in static HTML; browser used for screenshots only)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (EHI section is inline on the page, scroll to find it)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but no blocking)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone significant. The page loaded cleanly via curl and in the browser. All linked files downloaded without authentication or special headers. The only complication is that the EHI export documentation is entirely inline on the page rather than in a downloadable document, making it easy to miss among the other certification content. There are no images embedded in the EHI section (no screenshots of the export interface), though the text describes the UI workflow steps.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01SCND9SJ3zMy2kKUZN9itge","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Collection complete. Here's a summary:\n\n**Patagonia Health EHR — EHI Export Documentation Collection**\n\n**What was found:** The EHI export documentation is entirely inline on the ONC certification page (~400 words). No separate downloadable spec, data dictionary, or schema exists for the EHI export itself.\n\n**Export mechanism:**\n- **Clinical data:** CCDA 2.1 (USCDI v1) XML, exported per-patient or multi-patient via the Reports section\n- **Billing data:** Separate workflow via Billing > Claims, exported as CSV/XLSX/PDF\n- Access is role-based (Practice Admin enables EHI Export permission)\n\n**Key finding — (b)(10) vs (g)(10) confusion:** The clinical EHI export is constrained to CCDA 2.1 / USCDI v1, which covers the same standard clinical summary data as the (g)(10) FHIR API. For a public health and behavioral health EHR that stores communicable disease surveillance, contact tracing, behavioral health assessments, DSM-5 coded data, vaccine inventory, program compliance data, custom clinical templates, and more — CCDA is a poor fit that leaves many data domains undocumented and likely unexported. The billing export is a good sign (acknowledges EHI is broader than clinical summaries), but has zero format documentation.\n\n**Files collected:** 10 files including the full page HTML, extracted EHI section HTML, 3 PDFs (Patient Data API, SmartOnFHIR API, costs/limitations), 1 JSON (FHIR base URLs), and 4 screenshots."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":272,"cache_read_input_tokens":75743,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":272},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"73fc8d68-b8a9-41da-9c7d-3cf2038924ab","uuid":"c447254e-fdc4-4444-81bf-6f7776e12b90"}
